We're huge fans of Sentry and have it deeply integrated in our products. The fully open source nature has helped us a ton with these advanced integrations, being able to look at the code to see exactly what is happening instead of relying on docs.
I have run the self-hosted version of Sentry for a couple years at my job now and it has worked fantastically... The self-hosted version is rock-solid once running, I never worry about it.

This is a very disappointing development. I was hoping to implement Sentry for a side project I have been working on, now I will have to find an alternative or use an old version, as I refuse to rely on closed-source software.
I built Cabin as an alternative to Sentry. Less bloat, no vendor lock-in, works with any logger.
Each release would unleash more containers and consume more memory until we couldn't run anything on the 32gb server except Sentry.
We run them both as we are evaluating glitchtip, but, at least for us, it has so many bugs vs sentry. But it's so much lighter so we try to stick with it.
GlitchTip had replaced our Sentry (9.x, pre-Clickhouse madness)... it does 99% of what Sentry did with 10% of the effort to maintain a modern Sentry setup.

I know for a fact that your competition is using your code, even where they've built a differentiated service, e.g. Embrace is using Sentry Symbolicator... I'm not seeing what looks like too many, if any, outside contributions.
Building stuff for primarily developers is not easy, and I think they are doing great in that front.
I didn't know about Sentry origins as django-db-log. This was a good read, I had the pleasure of interacting from a few people at Sentry and they really seem like a cool group of people.
